newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU tightens controls on grain shipments.
newsitem.headline: EU tightens controls on grain shipments.

text.p: The European Union has agreed that exporters must give proof of arrival for grain shipments of more than 1,500 tonnes benefiting from differentiated export refunds, EU member state officials said.

The decision, taken at Thursday's meeting of the EU cereals management committee, modifies EU regulation 1501/95 and mainly affects sales to Morocco, Algeria and other North African countries for which special refund rates are set.
The aim is to tighten controls on grain shipments and to ensure that export refunds are used for the correct destination.
Exporters will continue to have to provide proof of arrival for grain shipments of less than 1,500 tonnes.
The European Commission is expected to change aid payment rules for farmers growing cereals and oilseeds on set-aside land for industrial uses, the officials added.
They said the Commission would press ahead even though the cereals committee was unable to give an opinion on a proposal to change regulation 334/93.
A compromise text contained some improvements but failed to secure the required weighted majority.
Farmers will now only be penalised if their yields are more than 10 percent, instead of five percent, below EU representative yields.
Greater flexibility will also be allowed in contracts between producers and processors. For instance seed varieties will not have to be specified.
